docs.title: PSA Intelligence Impersonate Proxy
docs.text:
HTTP/HTTPS proxy that impersonates browser TLS fingerprints using curl_cffi that can be effective in avoiding blocks against non-browser clients.

Attribution

This project started as a fork of hauxir/tls-impersonate-proxy and has now evolved beyond a pull request to merge. This impersonate-proxy project is maintained at psaintelligence/impersonate-proxy.

Pypi: pypi.org/project/impersonate-proxy

GHCR: github.com/psaintelligence/impersonate-proxy/pkgs/container

docs.title: Quick Start (Docker)
docs.text:
Spin up the proxy container:

docker run --rm -p 8899:8899 \
  -v /tmp/impersonate-certs:/home/impersonate/.config/impersonate-proxy \
  ghcr.io/psaintelligence/impersonate-proxy:latest

Once started, configure your client to trust the CA and use the proxy:

# Export the generated CA cert to trust the proxy
export SSL_CERT_FILE=/tmp/impersonate-certs/ca.crt

# Issue request through the proxy
curl --silent -x http://127.0.0.1:8899 https://tls.browserleaks.com/json

docs.title: Quick Start (pip / uv)
docs.text:
Install and start the proxy locally:

# Install via pipx from pypi
pipx install impersonate-proxy

# Or install via uv from source
uv pip install git+https://github.com/psaintelligence/impersonate-proxy.git

# Start the proxy (default: 127.0.0.1:8899)
impersonate-proxy

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• TLS Impersonation: Disguises client TLS fingerprints as standard browsers (Chrome or Firefox via curl_cffi >= 0.17.0).
  • Header Adapter & Delegation: Strips conflicting non-browser client headers (e.g. User-Agent: python-httpx and the full Sec-CH-UA-* family) so native curl-impersonate profile defaults shine through, while preserving payload, auth, and multi-cookie semantics.
  • Realistic Fingerprinting: Injects a platform-coherent full-build User-Agent with the complete Sec-CH-UA family, authentic Chromium GREASE brand lists, and canonical HTTP/2 header order for Chrome targets — and a UA-only full-build User-Agent for Firefox targets — on top of curl_cffi's TLS impersonation (on by default, --no-fingerprint-real to disable).
  • Access Control & SSRF Guardrails: Optional Basic proxy authentication (--proxy-auth), client allowlist (--allow-from), target deny list (--block-host), MITM-bypass raw-tunnel list (--raw-tunnel-host), and private-network egress blocking (--block-private-ips), with @/path/to/file lists and SIGHUP live reload.
  • Connection Keep-Alive, CurlShare & Custom DNS: Pools stateless curl_cffi sessions (discard_cookies=True, trust_env=False) backed by a shared DNS + TLS session cache (CurlShare), optional custom DNS / DoH (--dns), --max-threads handler cap, structured JSON logging (--log-format json), local /healthz liveness probe, and Prometheus /metrics (--stats-port) with latency histograms and active-thread gauges.
  • Fast Dynamic Cert Generation: Dynamic certificate generation using fast Elliptic Curve (ECDSA P-256) cryptography with leaf key reuse and an expiring LRU SSLContext cache.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Capability What it does Benefit TLS Fingerprinting Matches JA3/JA4/HTTP2 fingerprints with real browsers Defeats Cloudflare, Akamai, and Imperva WAF blocks MITM CONNECT Decryption Decrypts and re-signs HTTPS traffic using local CA (with --raw-tunnel-host bypass) Allows inspection, header filtering, and proxying of TLS streams while supporting pinned/WebSocket hosts Header Delegation Strips non-browser headers and delegates to curl-impersonate Ensures User-Agent and TLS fingerprint profiles align natively without duplication Client-Hint Coherence Full-build UA + complete Sec-CH-UA family with authentic GREASE in canonical HTTP/2 header order (Chrome); UA-only curation for Firefox Removes the scrubbed-UA / partial-client-hint tells that fingerprint services flag Access Control & SSRF Guardrails Optional --proxy-auth, --allow-from, --block-host, --block-private-ips, and SIGHUP file reload Runs the proxy as a controlled, multi-user-safe egress point Session Pooling & CurlShare Stateless pooled curl_cffi sessions with shared DNS + TLS session resumption and optional --dns / DoH Boosts throughput without cross-client cookie leakage or proxy env loops P-256 Cryptography Reuses a static leaf private key with a true LRU + pre-expiry cert cache Keeps leaf cert issuance <1ms and avoids serving expired certs in long-lived containers Observability & Limits Prometheus /metrics (counters, active threads, latency histogram), --log-format json, local /healthz, and --max-threads Monitors traffic live, integrates with log/container tooling, and prevents resource exhaustion

docs.title: Installation & CLI Guide
docs.text: impersonate-proxy can be run either as a local Python application or containerized using Docker.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or newer
  • pip or uv package manager
# Install via pipx from pypi
pipx install impersonate-proxy

# Or install via uv from source
uv pip install git+https://github.com/psaintelligence/impersonate-proxy.git

# Start the proxy (default: 127.0.0.1:8899)
impersonate-proxy

docs.title: Docker Installation (Recommended)
docs.text:
Running the proxy via Docker is recommended for isolated operation and to persist certificate states easily.

docker run --rm -p 8899:8899 \
  -v /tmp/impersonate-certs:/home/impersonate/.config/impersonate-proxy \
  ghcr.io/psaintelligence/impersonate-proxy:latest

The container runs as a dedicated non-root user (impersonate) and ships a HEALTHCHECK that probes both the local loopback /healthz endpoint and an end-to-end proxied request to Microsoft's lightweight connectivity probe (http://edge-http.microsoft.com/captiveportal/generate_204). Override the target with IMPERSONATE_PROXY_HEALTHCHECK_URL (or set it to "" for air-gapped deployments to run /healthz only).

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
You can spin up the service in the background using docker-compose: 

services:
  proxy:
    image: ghcr.io/psaintelligence/impersonate-proxy:latest
    ports:
      - "8899:8899"
    environment:
      - IMPERSONATE_PROXY_IMPERSONATE=chrome
      - IMPERSONATE_PROXY_DEBUG=false
    volumes:
      - impersonate-proxy-ca-certs:/home/impersonate/.config/impersonate-proxy

volumes:
  impersonate-proxy-ca-certs:

docs.title: Command Line Interface (CLI)
docs.text:
Run impersonate-proxy --help to view all available parameters:

usage: impersonate-proxy [-h] [--port PORT] [--host HOST]
                         [--impersonate IMPERSONATE] [--cffi-defaults |
                         --passthrough-headers] [--strip-client-leak-headers]
                         [--upstream-proxy UPSTREAM_PROXY] [--dns DNS]
                         [--no-fingerprint-real]
                         [--session-pool-max SESSION_POOL_MAX]
                         [--connect-timeout CONNECT_TIMEOUT]
                         [--read-timeout READ_TIMEOUT]
                         [--max-body-size MAX_BODY_SIZE]
                         [--tunnel-idle-timeout TUNNEL_IDLE_TIMEOUT]
                         [--block-host BLOCK_HOST]
                         [--raw-tunnel-host RAW_TUNNEL_HOST]
                         [--block-private-ips] [--proxy-auth PROXY_AUTH]
                         [--allow-from ALLOW_FROM] [--stats-port STATS_PORT]
                         [--max-threads MAX_THREADS]
                         [--log-format {text,json}] [--ca-dir CA_DIR]
                         [--debug] [--quiet]

HTTP/HTTPS proxy that impersonates browser TLS fingerprints

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --port, -p PORT       Port to listen on (default: 8899 or
                        IMPERSONATE_PROXY_PORT)
  --host, -H HOST       Host to bind to (default: 127.0.0.1 or
                        IMPERSONATE_PROXY_HOST)
  --impersonate, -i IMPERSONATE
                        Browser to impersonate (chrome, firefox, etc. Default:
                        chrome or IMPERSONATE_PROXY_IMPERSONATE)
  --cffi-defaults       Strip browser-shape headers (User-Agent, Sec-Ch-Ua-*,
                        Accept-Encoding, Priority, TE, Upgrade-Insecure-
                        Requests, Sec-Fetch-User) from the client and drop
                        bot-tell headers (Cache-Control, DNT, Connection) so
                        curl_cffi injects the correct current browser values
                        from its impersonation profile. [DEFAULT]
  --passthrough-headers
                        Forward client headers untouched; curl_cffi only sets
                        TLS-impersonation headers. For advanced users.
  --strip-client-leak-headers
                        Drop middlebox-chain / tracing leak headers
                        (X-Forwarded-*, Forwarded, Via, X-Request-ID,
                        X-Correlation-ID). CDN-ingress headers (X-Real-IP,
                        True-Client-IP, etc.) are forwarded with a warning
                        when present. Combinable with any header mode. Or
                        IMPERSONATE_PROXY_STRIP_CLIENT_LEAK_HEADERS=true
  --upstream-proxy UPSTREAM_PROXY
                        Upstream egress proxy URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8080
                        or IMPERSONATE_PROXY_UPSTREAM_PROXY)
  --dns DNS             Custom upstream DNS server IP(s) (comma-separated,
                        e.g. 1.1.1.1,8.8.8.8) or DNS-over-HTTPS URL (e.g.
                        https://1.1.1.1/dns-query). Or IMPERSONATE_PROXY_DNS
  --no-fingerprint-real
                        Disable injection of platform-coherent full-build UA +
                        complete Sec-CH-UA family on top of curl_cffi's TLS
                        impersonation. On by default in cffi-defaults mode. Or
                        IMPERSONATE_PROXY_FINGERPRINT_REAL=false
  --session-pool-max SESSION_POOL_MAX
                        Maximum reusable curl_cffi sessions in pool (default:
                        32 or IMPERSONATE_PROXY_SESSION_POOL_MAX)
  --connect-timeout CONNECT_TIMEOUT
                        Upstream TCP/TLS connect timeout in seconds (default:
                        10.0 or IMPERSONATE_PROXY_CONNECT_TIMEOUT)
  --read-timeout READ_TIMEOUT
                        Upstream HTTP read timeout in seconds (default: 300.0
                        or IMPERSONATE_PROXY_READ_TIMEOUT)
  --max-body-size MAX_BODY_SIZE
                        Maximum client request body accepted per request, in
                        bytes (default: 536870912 = 512 MiB or
                        IMPERSONATE_PROXY_MAX_BODY_SIZE). Larger bodies are
                        rejected with 413
  --tunnel-idle-timeout TUNNEL_IDLE_TIMEOUT
                        Idle seconds allowed on tunnel sockets before closing:
                        the raw-tunnel select loop and the MITM keep-alive
                        loop between requests (default: 30.0 or
                        IMPERSONATE_PROXY_TUNNEL_IDLE_TIMEOUT)
  --block-host BLOCK_HOST
                        Comma-separated target hostnames to refuse with 403
                        (exact or suffix match: example.com also blocks
                        *.example.com; prefix @/path/to/file for SIGHUP-
                        reloadable lists). Or IMPERSONATE_PROXY_BLOCK_HOST
  --raw-tunnel-host RAW_TUNNEL_HOST
                        Comma-separated target hostnames to bypass MITM and
                        relay via raw TCP tunnel on CONNECT (exact or suffix
                        match; supports @/path/to/file and SIGHUP reload). Or
                        IMPERSONATE_PROXY_RAW_TUNNEL_HOST
  --block-private-ips   Refuse requests targeting private, loopback, link-
                        local (cloud metadata), CGNAT, ULA, or multicast IP
                        addresses with 403 (SSRF protection). Or
                        IMPERSONATE_PROXY_BLOCK_PRIVATE_IPS=true
  --proxy-auth PROXY_AUTH
                        Require Proxy-Authorization: Basic auth with these
                        user:password credentials on every request; reply 407
                        otherwise (e.g. --proxy-auth alice:s3cret or
                        IMPERSONATE_PROXY_PROXY_AUTH)
  --allow-from ALLOW_FROM
                        Comma-separated client allowlist: bare IPs (matched
                        via the /24 or /64 auto-netblock, e.g. 192.168.1.7) or
                        explicit CIDRs (e.g. 10.0.0.0/8; supports
                        @/path/to/file and SIGHUP reload); other clients are
                        refused with 403. Or IMPERSONATE_PROXY_ALLOW_FROM
  --stats-port STATS_PORT
                        Serve Prometheus metrics at /metrics on this port (off
                        by default, or IMPERSONATE_PROXY_STATS_PORT)
  --max-threads MAX_THREADS
                        Maximum concurrent handler threads; excess connections
                        wait in the listen backlog (default: 0 = unlimited, or
                        IMPERSONATE_PROXY_MAX_THREADS)
  --log-format {text,json}
                        Log output format: 'text' (default) or 'json'. Or
                        IMPERSONATE_PROXY_LOG_FORMAT
  --ca-dir, -c CA_DIR   Directory to store/load CA certificate and key
                        (default: ~/.config/impersonate-proxy or
                        IMPERSONATE_PROXY_CA_DIR)
  --debug, -d           Enable verbose debug logging (unredacts URLs/hosts in
                        logs) or IMPERSONATE_PROXY_DEBUG=true
  --quiet, -q           Disable logging of request traffic or
                        IMPERSONATE_PROXY_QUIET=true

The two header-mode flags are mutually exclusive. The default mode is --cffi-defaults. Equivalent environment variables are IMPERSONATE_PROXY_HEADER_MODE (one of passthrough, cffi-defaults), IMPERSONATE_PROXY_STRIP_CLIENT_LEAK_HEADERS, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_UPSTREAM_PROXY, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_DNS, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_SESSION_POOL_MAX, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_READ_TIMEOUT, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_MAX_BODY_SIZE, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_TUNNEL_IDLE_TIMEOUT, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_BLOCK_HOST, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_RAW_TUNNEL_HOST, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_BLOCK_PRIVATE_IPS, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_PROXY_AUTH, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_ALLOW_FROM, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_STATS_PORT, IMPERSONATE_PROXY_MAX_THREADS, and IMPERSONATE_PROXY_LOG_FORMAT.

--block-host, --allow-from, and --raw-tunnel-host also accept @/path/to/file entries (one item per line, # comments ignored) and reload live on SIGHUP without interrupting active connections.

An unknown --impersonate target is rejected at startup (exit code 2) with a list of valid curl_cffi targets — it would otherwise fail lazily on the first request with a 502 and no actionable hint.

docs.title: Access Control & Routing (shared deployments)
docs.text:
The default bind is 127.0.0.1 (local only). When binding to a broader interface (--host 0.0.0.0, Docker), orthogonal guardrails keep the proxy from acting as an unauthenticated open relay or SSRF pivot:

# Require Basic proxy authentication (client: curl -x http://alice:s3cret@127.0.0.1:8899)
impersonate-proxy --host 0.0.0.0 --proxy-auth alice:s3cret

# Restrict clients, block SSRF targets, bypass MITM for pinned hosts, and reload lists on SIGHUP
impersonate-proxy --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --allow-from @/etc/impersonate-proxy/allow.txt \
  --block-host @/etc/impersonate-proxy/block.txt \
  --raw-tunnel-host @/etc/impersonate-proxy/pinned.txt \
  --block-private-ips \
  --dns https://1.1.1.1/dns-query \
  --log-format json
  • --proxy-auth checks Proxy-Authorization: Basic on both CONNECT and plain-HTTP requests in constant time; unauthorized clients receive 407 Proxy Authentication Required with a Proxy-Authenticate challenge.
  • --allow-from refuses clients outside the listed netblocks with 403.
  • --block-private-ips blocks requests targeting private, loopback, link-local (169.254.169.254), CGNAT, ULA, or multicast IP addresses with 403.
  • --raw-tunnel-host relays matched CONNECT hosts as raw TCP tunnels without MITM decryption (useful for certificate-pinned apps or WebSockets).
  • --block-host, --allow-from, and --raw-tunnel-host accept @/path/to/file lists and reload atomically on SIGHUP.
  • All guardrails are off by default; local usage and existing Docker flows are unchanged.

docs.title: Trusting the Root CA
docs.text:
To allow client applications to perform HTTPS requests through the proxy without throwing SSL verification errors:

  1. Locate the Certificate: By default, the root certificate is created at ~/.config/impersonate-proxy/ca.crt.
  2. Set Environment Variables: Many tools (like curl, wget, python-requests, httpx) respect specific environment variables for trust stores:
# Set CA trust path for curl
export SSL_CERT_FILE=~/.config/impersonate-proxy/ca.crt

# Set CA trust path for python-requests
export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=~/.config/impersonate-proxy/ca.crt

# Test HTTPS request through the proxy
curl -x http://127.0.0.1:8899 https://example.com

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
The repository ships a Makefile wrapping the common development tasks (all commands run through uv with an isolated virtualenv and cache):

make help            # List all available targets
make setup           # Create the isolated virtualenv and sync dependencies
make sync            # Sync python dependencies (dev environment)
make test            # Run offline unit and integration tests
make test-verbose    # Run offline tests with verbose output
make test-live       # Run basic live tests (hit real URLs)
make test-extended   # Run extended fingerprint/bot-detection live tests

make lint-fix        # Auto-fix linting and formatting issues

make bump-patch      # Bump the patch version number (e.g. 0.1.0 -> 0.1.1)
make bump-minor      # Bump the minor version number (e.g. 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0)

make docs-serve      # Serve documentation locally

Tests marked live / live_extended are deselected by default and require internet access; run them explicitly with make test-live / make test-extended.

docs.title: How It Works (Architecture & Workflow)
docs.text: impersonate-proxy acts as a transparent intermediary that sits between client applications (like curl, ffmpeg, or Python HTTP clients) and the destination servers. It prevents fingerprint blocking by aligning the client's TLS handshake fingerprint with its HTTP headers.

docs.title: 1. Request Interception Workflow
docs.text:
Below is a diagram illustrating how the proxy handles client requests:

sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as Client (e.g. curl)
    participant Proxy as Impersonate Proxy
    participant Target as Target Server (CDN/WAF)

    Client->>Proxy: HTTP request or HTTPS CONNECT
    alt Plain HTTP Request
        Proxy->>Proxy: Lease session from Pool
        Proxy->>Proxy: Adapt headers (Strip non-browser client overrides)
        Proxy->>Target: Issue request (via curl_cffi with TLS Impersonation)
        Target-->>Proxy: Response
        Proxy-->>Client: Stream response chunk-by-chunk
        Proxy->>Proxy: Return session to Pool
    else HTTPS CONNECT Request (MITM)
        Proxy-->>Client: HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established
        Proxy->>Proxy: Generate or lookup dynamic Leaf Cert
        Proxy->>Client: Perform local TLS Handshake (MITM)
        loop Keep-alive tunnel (until client closes or idle timeout)
            Client->>Proxy: Encrypted HTTP request
            Proxy->>Proxy: Lease session from Pool
            Proxy->>Proxy: Adapt headers (Strip non-browser client overrides)
            Proxy->>Target: Issue request (via curl_cffi with TLS Impersonation)
            Target-->>Proxy: Response
            Proxy-->>Client: Stream response chunk-by-chunk
            Proxy->>Proxy: Return session to Pool
        end
    end

docs.title: 2. Dynamic Certificate Generation (MITM)
docs.text:
For HTTPS requests, the proxy establishes a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) state to inspect headers and decrypt the client payload.

  1. Root CA Generation: At startup, if no CA files are found, the proxy creates a root CA private key and self-signed certificate using fast ECDSA SECP256R1 (P-256) keys.
  2. Leaf Certificate Issuance:
    • For each requested domain, the proxy generates a leaf certificate signed by the root CA.
    • Optimization: To avoid CPU bottleneck during RSA key creation, the proxy generates an ECDSA P-256 leaf certificate and reuses a single static leaf key (ctx.leaf_key) per proxy context across all generated certs. This reduces leaf cert generation times to <1ms.
  3. Certificate Caching: Generated ssl.SSLContext structures are stored in a thread-safe LRU cache (ctx.host_cert_cache) with pre-expiry refresh (29-day TTL for 30-day leaf certs). If the cache grows beyond 256 hosts, the least recently used (LRU) context is evicted automatically.

docs.title: 3. Keep-Alive Connection & Session Pooling
docs.text:
Under load (such as bursts of ~100 concurrent requests), initiating new curl_cffi sessions is resource-intensive due to easy handle allocation and TLS handshakes.

  • Context Session Pool: Each ProxyContext manages a queue-based ctx.session_pool containing reusable curl_cffi sessions (capped at 32 by default). Sessions are created with discard_cookies=True, trust_env=False, and a shared CurlShare(connect=False, dns=True, ssl_session=True) so pooled handles share DNS + TLS session resumption across threads without leaking cookies or looping through ambient proxy environment variables. Custom DNS servers or DNS-over-HTTPS (--dns) can be configured per instance.
  • Upstream Keep-Alive: Reusing sessions maintains active TCP connections to target hosts. Subsequent requests to the same target domain completely bypass DNS resolving and TCP/TLS handshake steps.
  • Resource Leasing: When a request starts, a session is leased from the pool. The proxy wraps the response's close() method so that the session is automatically returned to the pool only when the response stream has been fully consumed or closed by the client.
  • Handler Thread Cap: --max-threads N (env IMPERSONATE_PROXY_MAX_THREADS, default 0 = unlimited) bounds the concurrent handler threads with a semaphore; when the cap is reached the accept loop blocks and excess connections wait in the TCP listen backlog until a slot frees.

docs.title: Keep-alive CONNECT tunnels (client side)
docs.text:
Inside a decrypted CONNECT tunnel, the proxy honors client-driven keep-alive: after each response it loops to read the next request on the same TLS session instead of tearing the tunnel down, so browsers pay one TLS handshake per tunnel rather than one per request.

  • Client-driven persistence: HTTP/1.1 requests keep the tunnel open unless the client sends Connection: close; HTTP/1.0 requests require an explicit Connection/Proxy-Connection: keep-alive token. The response mirrors the decision (Connection: keep-alive or Connection: close).
  • Idle cap: a tunnel is dropped when the next request does not arrive within --tunnel-idle-timeout seconds (default 30.0, env IMPERSONATE_PROXY_TUNNEL_IDLE_TIMEOUT). The same knob bounds the raw-tunnel select loop.
  • Iteration cap: a hard cap (1000 requests) per tunnel guards against pathological clients.
  • Error handling inside the tunnel: an oversized request body (see below) is answered with 413, malformed framing with 400, and both end the tunnel; an upstream failure is answered with 502 and also ends the tunnel.

docs.title: Request body limit
docs.text: The proxy caps the client request body it will buffer, per request: --max-body-size bytes (default 536870912 = 512 MiB, env IMPERSONATE_PROXY_MAX_BODY_SIZE). This applies to both Content-Length bodies and de-chunked Transfer-Encoding: chunked bodies on both the plain-HTTP and MITM paths. Requests exceeding the cap are rejected with 413 Payload Too Large without buffering the body, and invalid/negative Content-Length values are rejected with 400.

docs.title: Target host controls & SSRF protection
docs.text:
• --block-host example.com,ads.example.net (env IMPERSONATE_PROXY_BLOCK_HOST) refuses requests to listed hostnames with 403 Forbidden — before any tunnel is established (CONNECT) or upstream request is issued (plain HTTP). Matching is case-insensitive and suffix-aware: an entry example.com blocks example.com itself and every *.example.com subdomain, but not notexample.com.
  • --raw-tunnel-host pinned.example.com (env IMPERSONATE_PROXY_RAW_TUNNEL_HOST) bypasses MITM decryption on CONNECT and relays raw TCP bytes instead (useful for certificate-pinned apps or WebSocket endpoints), while still honoring --allow-from, --proxy-auth, --block-host, and --block-private-ips.
  • --block-private-ips (env IMPERSONATE_PROXY_BLOCK_PRIVATE_IPS=true) blocks requests targeting private, loopback, link-local (169.254.169.254 cloud metadata), CGNAT, ULA, or multicast IP addresses (including hostnames resolving to them) with 403.
  • --block-host, --allow-from, and --raw-tunnel-host accept @/path/to/file entries and reload live on SIGHUP.

docs.title: 3b. Open-Proxy Guardrails
docs.text:
By default the proxy binds to 127.0.0.1 and requires neither authentication nor client access control. When exposing it on a broader interface (--host 0.0.0.0, Docker), two orthogonal flags keep it from acting as an unauthenticated open relay:

  • --proxy-auth user:password (env IMPERSONATE_PROXY_PROXY_AUTH): every CONNECT and plain-HTTP request must carry Proxy-Authorization: Basic <token> matching the configured credentials (verified in constant time via hmac.compare_digest). Unauthorized clients receive 407 Proxy Authentication Required with a Proxy-Authenticate challenge — for CONNECT this happens before 200 Connection established, so no tunnel is ever opened for unauthenticated clients.
  • --allow-from (env IMPERSONATE_PROXY_ALLOW_FROM): a comma-separated client allowlist. Entries are either bare IPs — matched via the same /24 (IPv4) or /64 (IPv6) auto-netblock used in logging — or explicit CIDR netblocks (10.0.0.0/8). Clients outside the list receive 403; an unverifiable client address is denied while an allowlist is active.

Both are off by default: local usage and existing Docker flows are unchanged.

docs.title: 3c. Optional Stats Endpoint (Prometheus)
docs.text:
--stats-port PORT (env IMPERSONATE_PROXY_STATS_PORT, off by default) starts a tiny HTTP server serving Prometheus text-format metrics at /metrics, bound to the same host as the proxy:

Metric Type Meaning impersonate_proxy_requests_total{mode=...} counter Client requests forwarded upstream, by mode (plain_http, mitm, raw_tunnel) impersonate_proxy_upstream_failures_total counter Upstream requests that failed before producing a response (surfaced to the client as 502) impersonate_proxy_client_status_total{status_class=...} counter Client-facing responses with status ≥ 400, by class (4xx/5xx) — includes early rejects (400/403/407/413) impersonate_proxy_session_pool_high_water gauge Maximum concurrently leased curl_cffi sessions impersonate_proxy_active_threads gauge Handler threads currently serving client connections impersonate_proxy_request_duration_seconds histogram Upstream request handling latency in seconds impersonate_proxy_cert_cache_size gauge Host SSL contexts currently cached

Structured JSON logs can also be enabled with --log-format json (IMPERSONATE_PROXY_LOG_FORMAT=json).

Counters are always active (negligible overhead); only the HTTP endpoint is gated behind the flag.

impersonate-proxy --stats-port 9100 &
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics

docs.title: 4. Header Modes
docs.text: This is one of the most important — and often overlooked — mechanisms in the proxy. It is what makes the difference between bypassing a WAF and getting blocked.

docs.title: Why it matters
docs.text:
WAF/CDN systems such as Cloudflare, Akamai, and Imperva perform two independent fingerprinting checks:

  1. TLS fingerprint (JA3/JA4): based on the SSL ClientHello — cipher suites, extensions, elliptic curves, etc.
  2. HTTP header fingerprint: based on the presence and ordering of HTTP headers — User-Agent, Accept, Accept-Language, Accept-Encoding, Sec-Fetch-*, and Chrome Client Hints (Sec-Ch-Ua-*).

curl_cffi handles the TLS side flawlessly by using libcurl patched with browser fingerprints. However, if you send a curl/7.81.0 User-Agent or omit Sec-Fetch-Dest headers, the WAF sees a TLS handshake that says "Chrome 120" and headers that say "curl" — an immediate mismatch that triggers a block.

The proxy therefore exposes two mutually-exclusive header modes plus an orthogonal client-leak stripping flag. The key insight: curl_cffi already injects the full current browser header set when default_headers=True (the project's default). The proxy's job is to get out of curl_cffi's way — strip client-supplied browser-shape headers that would override curl_cffi's defaults, and let curl_cffi own the rest.

docs.title: The two header modes
docs.text: Mode Flag Env var Behaviour cffi-defaults (default) --cffi-defaults IMPERSONATE_PROXY_HEADER_MODE=cffi-defaults Strip browser-shape headers (User-Agent, Sec-Ch-Ua-*, Accept-Encoding, Priority, TE, Upgrade-Insecure-Requests, Sec-Fetch-User) from the client so curl_cffi injects the correct current browser values; drop bot-tell headers (Cache-Control, DNT, Connection); preserve request-specific headers (Cookie, Authorization, Referer, Content-Type, If-*, Range, Host) and shape-dependent headers (Accept, Sec-Fetch-Dest/Mode/Site, real Accept-Language). passthrough --passthrough-headers IMPERSONATE_PROXY_HEADER_MODE=passthrough Forward client headers untouched (curl_cffi only manages TLS). You are fully responsible for header/TLS consistency. For advanced users.

docs.title: --strip-client-leak-headers (orthogonal)
docs.text:
Drops middlebox-chain and tracing headers that a client may realistically forward and that betray the request as coming through a proxy or non-browser client. Combinable with any header mode:

  • X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Server
  • Forwarded (RFC 7239)
  • Via
  • X-Request-ID, X-Correlation-ID

Env var: IMPERSONATE_PROXY_STRIP_CLIENT_LEAK_HEADERS=true.

CDN-ingress headers are not stripped. Headers such as X-Real-IP, True-Client-IP, CF-Connecting-IP, X-Cluster-Client-IP, and Fastly-Client-IP are normally added by a CDN/edge layer on ingress to the CDN — they should never appear in a client request. If one is present, it indicates a misconfiguration (or replay of captured traffic); the proxy logs a warning and forwards it unchanged so the misconfig is visible to the operator rather than silently swallowed.

docs.title: How cffi-defaults works
docs.text:
curl_cffi (with default_headers=True, the project's default) automatically injects the complete current browser header set from its impersonation profile — User-Agent, Sec-Ch-Ua-*, Sec-Fetch-*, Accept, Accept-Encoding, Accept-Language, Priority, TE — matching the curl-impersonate captured signatures for chrome152 / firefox155 exactly.

Critical behaviour: client-supplied headers OVERRIDE curl_cffi's defaults. So forwarding a client's Accept: */* or Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate silently breaks impersonation — curl_cffi cannot fix it.

cffi_defaults_headers() therefore:

  1. Strips browser-shape headers the client should not own (User-Agent, the full Sec-Ch-Ua* family, Accept-Encoding, Upgrade-Insecure-Requests, Sec-Fetch-User, Priority, TE) so curl_cffi's profile defaults and curated fingerprints shine through.
  2. Drops bot-tell headers (Cache-Control, DNT, Connection — the last with a warning because curl_cffi manages HTTP/2 connection state itself).
  3. Strips Accept-Language only when the client sent the literal * (a bot tell); real values like en-US,en;q=0.9 are preserved.
  4. Preserves everything else: request-specific headers (Host, Cookie, Authorization, Referer, Origin, Content-Type, Content-Length, If-Match, If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since, If-Unmodified-Since, Range) and shape-dependent headers curl_cffi cannot infer — Accept (nav vs XHR), Sec-Fetch-Dest/Mode/Site. A non-browser XHR client (e.g. httpx) correctly sends Sec-Fetch-Mode: cors on its XHR requests; preserving it keeps the request XHR-shaped. Forcing curl_cffi's nav-style defaults onto an XHR request would itself be a bot tell.

The Chrome and Firefox header sets curl_cffi injects are sourced from the curl-impersonate signature files and track the latest default profiles (chrome152, firefox155 as of curl_cffi >= 0.17). The proxy no longer hardcodes them.

docs.title: The realistic client-hint override (--fingerprint-real, default on)
docs.text:
curl_cffi's impersonation profiles ship two residual tells that fingerprint services can detect:

  1. Scrubbed UA build — Chrome/152.0.0.0 instead of a real full build like Chrome/152.0.7977.83.
  2. Incomplete client-hint family — only the basic Sec-CH-UA triplet, missing Sec-CH-UA-Full-Version-List, Sec-CH-UA-Platform-Version, Sec-CH-UA-Arch, Sec-CH-UA-Bitness.

On top of curl_cffi's TLS profile, the proxy injects a curated, platform-coherent header fingerprint (fingerprint.py) for recognized Chrome targets: a full-build User-Agent plus the complete Sec-CH-UA-* family, with the UA platform token, Sec-CH-UA-Platform, and Sec-CH-UA-Platform-Version kept mutually consistent (a Windows UA with Sec-CH-UA-Platform: "macOS" is an instant bot tell).

Firefox targets (firefox155, and the bare firefox alias) are curated UA-only: Firefox sends no client hints and its UA carries no scrubbed-build tell (rv: always matches Firefox/), so the proxy pins a full platform-coherent UA on the most common desktop shape (Windows / Win64 / x64, consistent with the Chrome family default) and leaves curl_cffi's authentic captured HTTP/2 header order untouched — no header_order override is sent for Firefox.

It also fixes HTTP/2 header ordering: curl_cffi's profile sends the injected client hints in non-canonical order, so the proxy passes extra_fp={"header_order": ...} with Chrome's canonical wire order (client-hint family grouped, user-agent before accept, then the sec-fetch-* cluster). Header order is enforced at the HTTP/2 frame level — the order fingerprint services actually inspect.

Disable with --no-fingerprint-real or IMPERSONATE_PROXY_FINGERPRINT_REAL=false. The override is active only in cffi-defaults mode and only when a curated fingerprint exists for the target; unknown targets fall back to curl_cffi's untouched profile headers.

docs.title: Choosing a mode
docs.text:
cffi-defaults (default) — best for almost all clients, including non-browser httpx-style clients. Such a client sends Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate (no br/zstd), Cache-Control: no-cache, DNT: 1, and a python-httpx User-Agent. cffi-defaults strips all of those and lets curl_cffi inject the correct Chrome/Firefox equivalents, while preserving the client's Accept: */* and Sec-Fetch-Mode: cors so the request keeps its XHR shape.

# Recommended configuration for non-browser clients
impersonate-proxy --cffi-defaults --strip-client-leak-headers

# Or via env vars (cffi-defaults is the default, shown for completeness)
IMPERSONATE_PROXY_HEADER_MODE=cffi-defaults \
IMPERSONATE_PROXY_STRIP_CLIENT_LEAK_HEADERS=true \
impersonate-proxy

passthrough — for users who want full manual control. The proxy only handles TLS; you must ensure your client's HTTP headers are consistent with the impersonated TLS profile.

passthrough trade-offs

With --passthrough-headers, no header sanitisation happens. If your client sends a python-httpx User-Agent or omits Sec-Fetch-*, WAFs will block the request despite the impersonated TLS handshake.

docs.title: Passing your own headers
docs.text:
Custom X-* headers, Authorization, Cookie, Referer, Origin, Content-Type, If-*, and Range are preserved by both modes. To set a custom User-Agent that survives the proxy, use --passthrough-headers:

impersonate-proxy --passthrough-headers
curl -x http://127.0.0.1:8899 -H "User-Agent: MyApp/2.0" https://example.com

With --cffi-defaults (default), the User-Agent is always stripped so curl_cffi injects the impersonated profile's browser UA.

docs.title: 5. Sensitive Header Redaction in Logs
docs.text: The proxy redacts sensitive headers (e.g. Authorization, Cookie, X-Api-Key) from log output by default. Full header values are only logged when --debug mode is active.
